activities.description: Aerial view of rural area with text overlay "LOTTS CREEK, KENTUCKY".
Coach Osborne dribbling a basketball in an empty gym.
Player 1 leaning against a wall looking distressed.
Coach Osborne continues dribbling and speaks about helping kids through sports.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The scene sets the stage for the narrative, highlighting Coach Osborne's mission to inspire and uplift his players.

mood.description: Determined, Hopeful. Coach Osborne's voice and words suggest determination and hope, contrasting with Player 1's distressed expression.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Transition from the Coach's hopeful expression to Player 1's distress introduces a sense of concern.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction to Coach Osborne's mission and the challenges faced by the youth he aims to help.

scenes.thematicElements: Hope, sports as a vehicle for change, overcoming adversity.
scenes.title: Introduction in Lotts Creek

videoEditingDetails.description: Slow zoom out from aerial view.
Intercutting between Coach Osborne speaking and Player 1 looking distressed.
Fade to black. "UPROXX PRESENTS" text overlay.

activities.description: White Man 1 leans against a basketball hoop and smiles.
Cut to black. Text overlay "AN ORIGINAL DOCUMENTARY SERIES."

scenes.contextualRelevance: Highlights the racial dynamics within the community, setting the stage for the conflicts to come.

mood.description: Tense, Uneasy. The White Man's demeanor and the statement "predominantly white area" create tension, hinting at racial dynamics.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The statement "predominantly white area" introduces an undercurrent of racial tension, shifting the mood.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduces the setting and hints at racial dynamics within the community.

scenes.title: Introduction to the Community

activities.description: Exterior shot of a house with a Confederate flag.
A man states, "They don't wanna be beat by black boys." Cut to a basketball team (mixed race) celebrating.
Player 1 speaks about being different.
Shots of audio equipment and Radio Host talks about players being recruited based on race.
Player 2 spins a basketball and throws it towards the hoop.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Illustrates the direct impact of racial prejudice on the community and team dynamics.

mood.description: Tense, Frustrated, Determined. The Confederate flag and the man's comment establish a racially charged environment. The Players and Coach Osborne, however, seem determined to succeed despite the prejudice.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The Confederate flag immediately injects a tense atmosphere.
The shift from the tense statement to the joyful celebration of the diverse team creates a powerful contrast, highlighting the team's defiance.
The Radio Host's words escalate the tension by confirming the presence of racial bias in recruitment.

narrativeProgression.description: This scene exposes the racism and prejudice within the community and its impact on the team and coach.

scenes.title: Facing Racial Tensions

videoEditingDetails.description: Slow pan across the house exterior.
Abrupt cut to the basketball team celebrating.
Fast cuts between different shots of players, radio host, and basketball games.

activities.description: The basketball team stands in a huddle.
People in the crowd clap their hands.
Player 1 stands in front of a school bus. White Man 2 speaks about Player 1. Cut to a basketball game.
White Man 2 says, "If you can't do it with your own home kids, then get the hell out of basketball." A basketball game continues. A woman cheers.
A woman screams. News anchors speak about violence. Images of vandalism.

Players 1 & 2 look sad. White Woman 2 speaks about players being dressed up as gorillas. Images from social media. White Man 2 and another man speak about banning students from sports. A man asks, "Did this just happen?"
Coach Osborne sits on bleachers holding a basketball and looking dejected. A man asks, "How do you fire a coach that just won a state championship?"

scenes.contextualRelevance: Highlights the consequences of unchecked prejudice and the impact on the team's progress.

mood.description: Tense, Angry, Shocked, Heartbreaking. The scene rapidly escalates from tense competition to outrage as the racist attacks against the team and coach are revealed. The mood turns somber as Coach Osborne faces the consequences.

keyMoments.changeDescription: White Man 2's statement about "home kids" introduces open resentment towards the players.
The phrase "Get the hell out of basketball" marks a shift to aggressive hostility.
Transition to news reports and the woman's scream abruptly escalates the tension, signaling a turn towards real-world violence.
Images of vandalism and the gorilla costume intensify the sense of threat and injustice.
The abrupt shift to a quiet, contemplative shot of Coach Osborne, coupled with the question about his firing, creates a stark contrast, leaving a sense of sadness and injustice.

narrativeProgression.description: The situation spirals as racist attacks and threats escalate, leading to real-world consequences for the team and coach.

scenes.thematicElements: Escalating racism, community division, injustice, the price of success, resilience in the face of hate.
scenes.title: Escalation and Consequences

videoEditingDetails.description: Slow-motion shot of team and crowd.
Rapid cuts between different speakers, basketball games, and images.
Slow zoom in on Coach Osborne's face.

activities.description: Coach Osborne walks with his head down.
Coach Osborne addresses his team, telling them to use the hate they experience as fuel.
Shots of the basketball team running down a hallway, playing a game, cheerleaders cheering.
The team hugs Coach Osborne.
Fast cuts between basketball plays and the team chanting, "We got your back."
Coach Osborne and a player lead a crowd in dancing on a basketball court.

characterInteraction.description: Coach Osborne rallies and inspires his team; players show support and determination.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Demonstrates the power of unity and resilience against adversity.

mood.description: Determined, Hopeful, United. Despite facing adversity, the team rallies around Coach Osborne, channeling their anger and frustration into motivation.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Transition from Coach Osborne’s somber walk to him addressing the team with a determined expression signals a shift in attitude.
Coach Osborne’s words “Use it as fuel” mark a turning point, urging his team to turn negativity into strength.
The embrace between Coach Osborne and his players emphasizes unity and support in the face of adversity.

narrativeProgression.description: The team finds strength and unity in the face of hate, turning their experiences into motivation.

scenes.thematicElements: Unity, resilience, channeling anger into motivation, overcoming adversity, the power of support.
scenes.title: Unity and Resilience

videoEditingDetails.description: Slow-motion shot of Coach Osborne walking.
A mix of medium shots and close-ups, focusing on Coach Osborne's words and the team’s reactions.
Fast-paced cuts of game highlights and celebrations.

climax.description: The revelation that Coach Osborne is fired despite leading his team to a state championship marks the climax of the trailer.

storylines.description: Coach Osborne's journey to uplift a basketball team facing racism.

youtube_description:
When a black coach takes control of a high school basketball team in rural Kentucky, heads turn. When he wins, heads roll. UPROXX original documentary "Us Against The World" examines how Cordia High School became a hotbed for racial tension.  All 10 episodes of Us Against The World will be available to stream on September 19, exclusively on http://www.watchable.com/
